profile.headline: Software Engineer at Figma
profile.summary:
I am a biologist-turned-software engineer, a relentless problem solver and perpetual learner. I enjoy unraveling complex problems down to their essential parts to design and develop clean and functional products for end-users. 

Some of my favorite technologies are: Ruby on Rails, StimulusJS, React, HTML, CSS, Node, Express, MySQL/PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and Docker.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Built and deployed a survey tool in 1 month to successfully find over 40,000 plasma donation patients for COVID-19 research efforts.
• Designed, architected and rebuilt a new responsive and multi platform compatible screening tool using Ruby on Rails
  • Supported studies and screeners to find over 4,000 potential participants across multiple studies
  • Created varying portals for administrators, site coordinators, and sponsors to review participants and studies based on role permissions
  • Built analytics dashboards that allowed administrators to understand study performance
• Worked closely with the CEO and operations team to construct product roadmaps and organize weekly sprint and daily tasks
• Contributed to in house template repositories that reduced the time to bootstrap new client projects from 1 week to 1 day.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Worked closely with product and data science teams to design and implement fullstack applications with a ReactJS frontend and Kotlin middletier, including features such as a detailed timeline with a navigable breakdown of patient records
• Created a custom ORM to construct complex medically relevant queries that translate into Elasticsearch and Neo4j requests
• Assisted in architecting and writing an application that connects multiple hospital sites to a central hub using ETCD
• Established, published, and maintained internal reusable component library utilizing Storybook.js, with documentation and testing in Jest / Enzyme
• Lead engineer defining styles and conventions for application projects and regularly took part in code reviews
• Phonescreened, interviewed, wrote coding challenge assignments, and reviewed submissions to triple the size of the application team

positions.title: Hacker in Residence (Teaching Fellow)
positions.description:
• Mentor students in Javascript and Web Development fundamentals, engineering best practices, debugging, application design choices, and TDD
• Deliver lectures introducing technical interview topics such as data structures, dynamic programming, and essential Javascript concepts 
• Serve as Project Manager for student teams and provided guidance during the develop phase, including but not restricted to: code reviews to reinforce clean and modular code, designing and setting up databases with associations in multiple ORMs, and leading standups to optimize workflow and team cooperation
• Conduct technical and behavioral interviews with prospective students

positions.title: Private Tutor
positions.description:
• Taught Algebra I, Algebra II, Geometry, Precalculus, Calculus, Honors & AP Biology, Honors & AP Chem
• Improved grades of 100% of students

positions.title: Lab Assistant II
positions.description:
• Set up and established new lab and managed finances, ordering, and supply inventory
• Researched multiple areas related to intrauterine growth restriction and its implications in differential gene expression, primarily focusing on  circadian rhythm and metabolic changes
• Trained undergraduate volunteers and oversaw student experiments and projects

company.name: David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA

positions.title: Library Assistant II, Student Supervisor
positions.description:
• Managed library operations during nights, weekends, and holidays in absence of full time staff
• Supervised student workflow and helped implement efficient management methods
• Located hard copy and online scientific journals and articles for patrons

company.name: UCLA Louise M. Darling Biomedical Library

volunteerExperiences.description:
• Led two 10-day trips to Costa Rica (Sept 2009, 2010) & one 14-day trip to villages in Tibet (July 2012)
• Compiled information for dental, nutrition, and sanitation workshops and presented to communities
• Fundraised over $3000 per trip and managed activities, itinerary, and safety of the group while abroad
• Donated medical supplies, helped run food banks, build bunk beds, and facilitate a trash clean upday

• Assisted over thirty patients sign up for health insurance and various social services
• Learned how to interview patients, put together a differential diagnosis and write up SOAP notes

publications.title: The hepatic transcriptome of young suckling and aging intrauterine growth restricted male rats
